title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in this manuscript Grothendieck wants finite presentations (generators and relations) of Teichmüller groupoids. He builds them by 'dévissage': a groupoid of interest is the total category of a category fibered over a base groupoid or category S. This page finishes a general lemma giving a presentation of the total category (Grothendieck construction) ΓC of a fibered category C → S from three ingredients: presentations of the fibres, a presentation of the base, and the transport action.

Data, following the previous page:
(i) Fibre generators. In each fibre C̃_s there is a family of fibre arrows a_j. The hypothesis is that for each object s̃, the a_j that are loops at s̃ generate Aut_{C̃_s}(s̃), and the whole family generates the fibre category (corrected reading of the inserted line).
(ii) Lifts of base generators. Each generator u_i of the base is lifted to an arrow ũ_i (written u'_i on the previous page), a choice of transport arrow.
(iii) Relation (12), the lifted base relations. For each base relation α (a word u_{i_1}...u_{i_n} = 1 in S), the composite of the lifts lies over an identity, so it is a fibre arrow. It is therefore a word in the a_j. Relation (12) states that this word, inserted with the lifts, composes to the identity:
M_{α,1}((a_j)) u'_{i'_{α,1}} ... M_{α,n_α}((a_j)) u'_{i'_{α,n_α}} = 1.
(iv) Relation (13), the fibre relations. Relations N'_β((a_j)) = 1 that present each fibre category C̃_s on the generators a_j.
(v) Relation (14), the boxed relation. For each loop a_{j0} at s̃ and each u_i with source s̃, the transport ũ_i(a_{j0}) is expressed as a word M''_{i,j}((a_j)) in the target fibre. This is ũ_i a_{j0} ũ_i^{-1} = word, i.e. how the base generators act on fibre generators.

Claim: (12), (13) and (14) together form a system of defining relations for ΓC, i.e. a presentation of the total category.

This is the groupoid / fibered-category version of P. Hall's classical presentation of a group extension 1 → N → G → Q → 1. That presentation uses generators of N plus lifts of generators of Q, with three kinds of relations:
- the relations of N;
- conjugation relations expressing the action;
- lifted relations of Q set equal to words in N.

The intended application is presenting mapping-class / Teichmüller groupoids from fibrations such as forgetting a point (Birman-type sequences) or restriction to subsurfaces.
errors: No mathematical error, but the statement is only sketched. For a fibered category over a non-groupoid base, or a fibration that is not split, one must also handle the cleavage: identities and compositions of transports, i.e. relations ũ_{id} = word, plus the choice of transport arrows.

Relations (14) are only imposed for loops a_{j0}. For non-loop fibre generators one needs either that loops plus a connecting tree generate, or analogous relations. The hypothesis on the previous page ('les a_j qui sont des lacets en s̃ engendrent Aut') together with fibre generation suggests he has this in mind, but it is not written.

ideas.what: Presentation of the total category of a fibered category (over a groupoid) from presentations of the fibres, the base, and the transport action.
ideas.modern_name: Presentation of extensions (P. Hall), generalized to the Grothendieck construction / fibrations of groupoids
ideas.usually_credited_to: P. Hall (groups); R. Brown, P. J. Higgins and others for groupoid fibrations; used for mapping class group presentations by Birman, Hatcher–Thurston, Wajnryb
ideas.where_published: Not as such; Esquisse d'un programme (1984) only alludes to presenting the Teichmüller tower by generators and relations.

deep.surprise_reason: A standard (Hall-type) presentation lemma for extensions, transposed to fibered categories over groupoids as a tool for the Teichmüller tower. It is a useful technical step but well known in substance.
transcription_corrections: Line 3: 'a_{j0} qui est une base' should read 'a_{j0} qui est un lacet' (a loop). Likewise on the previous page, 'des buts en s̃' is likely 'des lacets en s̃'.
Line 4: 'que a = origine s̃ que j'ai une relation' should read 'qui a comme origine s̃, qu'on ait une relation'.
Last line: 'définissant pour TC' should read 'définissante pour ΓC' (the total category); the symbol is Γ, not T.
The underbrace annotation reads 'flèche de la catégorie fibre contenant cat.(ũ_i)' (i.e. the fibre over the target of u_i).
